how: Calls recruit members to begin, enlarge and repair the flag, with some reporting their contributions.
Limited room is weighed against an already legible flag rather than automatically prompting relocation.
A starter supplies a flag proposal and location that other participants answer with offers of help.
Participants negotiate placement, proportions, expansion and lettering rather than merely select a national symbol.
Requests for Godzilla, aircraft and sakura coexist with flag work without demonstrating one adopted replacement project.
Participants report clearing whitespace, rebuilding overnight and moving the sun or kanji.
Participants circulate coordinates and references, request one shared plan and give explicit alignment instructions.
Sharing automation code and requesting an accessible browser version form a preparatory step distinct from verified automated placement.
Code offers and requests do not establish that participants ran automation for this flag, while claims about neighbouring bots remain attributed reports.
This room cannot test a population frequency, and moderator posting rules do not establish a decided canvas organization.
Assess organization separately for the host discussion and pixel work because explicit moderator control of posting coexists with disclaimed responsibility for placement.
Template circulation alone does not establish settled design when participants still disagree about whether changes constitute expansion or ruin.
A circle generator still requires an agreed radius, and a circulated reference may require explicit alignment instructions.
Requests to move planning into chat encounter an explicitly reported lack of a room chat and a participant unable to create it.
Defenders rebuild through the night, postpone resizing and clean repeatedly changed pixels.
Participants distinguish vandalism from accidental placement and competing attempts to fix the flag.
A claim of coordinated attack is challenged and its author acknowledges having inferred coordination from individual placers.
Defensive strain and automation requests coexist, but actual automated placement and a demonstrated manual-capacity threshold remain unobserved.
A participant explicitly treats relief from vandalism as an opportunity to resume improvements if enough people join.
Participants ask defenders to spare a neighbour's red territory and affirm territorial respect.
The accuser apologizes for the attribution and reaffirms the mutual border rather than admitting a proven coordinated attack.
Neighbours offer border terms and a reported calm discussion resolves an overlap by obtaining agreement to move.
A participant reports talking with the overlapping group and obtaining its agreement without establishing authority over every placer.
Members solicit spare pixels and outside participants report helping defend the flag.
An accepted defence bargain is followed by inclusion on an allies list, establishing a bilateral alliance rather than a large council.
A border worker's defensive exchange leads to a reported conversation with the overlapping group and agreement to move.
An accepted border bargain is subsequently invoked through an instruction to leave the neighbour's red area alone.
An outside helper explicitly explains joining the defence by the flag's repeated vandalization.
Border restraint and defence are offered together in exchange for help clearing letters, without independently verifying fulfilment.
The offer to defend a threatened neighbour is accepted and becomes an allies-list entry.
A challenge to attack attribution receives an explicit acknowledgement of mistaken inference and renewed border respect.
Correcting an attack attribution and reaffirming the border are followed by a promise to recruit helpers and thanks.
The abandoned plan belongs to the visiting group, while the reported overlap resolution has that group move rather than the flag makers.
A title places a Japanese flag inside the French flag but supplies no hosting agreement or rule to test.
Accepting a defence agreement does not disclose a dispute over who can bind all placers.
The recorded border bargain has acceptance and alliance recognition but no ensuing challenge to treaty-making authority.
Homeland and motherland language frames recruitment as national belonging without establishing speakers' nationality or a political consensus.
Rising Sun and Finland jokes vary what counts as Japan on the canvas without establishing a historical cause of conflict.
Reports naming national attackers do not establish a quarrel carried over from before the canvas.
No cited turn connects a prior national tie to its own attack call, so national labels alone cannot instantiate this claim.
Moderators centralize discussion, threaten removal of other threads and disown responsibility for canvas activities.
The moderator explicitly explains stickying a thread as a response to repeated canvas posts.
Canvas jokes do not establish that the host community was keyed as an April Fools takeover.
Contributors thank defenders and celebrate completion while explicitly calling for continued protection.
A participant marks the effort over, but this does not establish a final preserved image or complete retrospective.
A completion announcement explicitly couples celebration with the need to protect the flag, making completion a maintenance threshold rather than a terminal state.
The closing congratulation supplies no decision to preserve ties, repurpose a venue or carry the work elsewhere.
Marking the effort over supplies no post-placement dispute over cleaned images or historical accounts.
A participant proposes invading space for sakura, establishing an attack proposal but not execution.
The declaration of defeating snek is a victory claim without independent verification of the opponent or outcome.
A direct response reports helping without a reciprocal demand.
The starter's call receives reports of helping, and later replies describe a legible flag.
The proposal supplies starting coordinates and an appeal for help in the same initiating turn.
A contributor's completion announcement explicitly identifies the finished flag as needing protection.
Reporting lettering work culminates in an explicit completion celebration within the same edited contribution.
A bare response supports one acceptance sequence but cannot establish that every reader owes an answer or that silent placing occurred.
The end remark and completion edits have no separate edit times or explicit link showing celebration caused preservation.
An end marker is present but no observed carrying-forward decision follows it.
A cramped alternative is rejected in favour of an existing legible flag, not followed by an observed relocation after defeat.
A later invasion proposal lacks a demonstrated path from recruitment to attacking placements.
The invasion proposal has no recorded refusal or apology in reply, and the separate attribution apology does not establish this sequence.
The attack accusation leads to a correction, but actual coordinated aggression is disputed rather than established as the origin of a new truce.
The victory claim lacks a documented initiating attack connecting it to a subsequent verbal contest.
Accepting the shared lettering space as good neighbourliness preserves the flag's red and white without requiring removal of the neighbouring name.
